label_review: Source-inspection curator declarations; independent review and final acceptance belong to the canonical parity ledger and exact-commit attestation.
selection: Two separately maintained primary projects, selected before scores; Requests calibration, Flask held out. No label, split, threshold target or minimum-support edits after scoring.
acquisition: Read-only bounded raw files from immutable primary-repository commits; tag metadata resolved via GitHub API. No project source or build configuration executed. No downloaded weights.
source_snapshots: .victor/sandbox/graph-project-calibration-20261102/{requests,flask} under the canonical workspace (workspace-owned ignored storage; six files and original frozen manifest copied and SHA-256 verified before handoff)
limitations: 24 new Python/Python structural pairs across two independent projects; not behavior, source-copy identity, refactor safety or whole-repository retrieval accuracy.
Many positive examples are small wrappers with correlated siblings; nominal pair Wilson bounds are not grouped uncertainty intervals.
No held-out project threshold or label tuning. Portable abstentions retained and no failed gate suppressed.
BGE general-purpose text representation has no feasible calibration policy on these labels; successful scoring/cache reuse does not qualify this model.
Single ARM64 host; run timings include source capture through report assembly, exclude startup/serialization, and RSS is process lifetime peak.
One repository per split and both Python HTTP ecosystems; each split has three positive family clusters and four units reused across multiple pairs.
Disjoint selected repository/family identities and file hashes do not prove broad source-lineage independence or statistical generalization.

The LookupDict positive explicitly abstracts declaration signatures and the explicit default operand origin (literal None versus caller argument), as disclosed by its original frozen rationale; no normalized-AST or interface identity is asserted.
